memory_update.text: BWXT should remain in the reference lane for nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks, but only as an inference until primary filings or DOE contract data show HALEU/deconversion/feedstock materiality.

GHM is a speculative shadow candidate for dispatchable-power and SMR balance-of-plant; survival to Layer 3 requires proof of material energy-generation orders rather than defense/space-driven backlog.
LTBR is best treated as a development-stage downstream advanced-fuel option, not a current infrastructure chokepoint owner.
ASPI has high thematic fit to isotope/enrichment scarcity but very low evidence quality until licensing, technical scale-up and commercial contract economics are validated.
MTZ maps to utility EPC and execution capacity, but it is a diversified reference name; segment backlog and margin mix must be checked before treating it as a grid bottleneck beneficiary.
PPSI is a micro-cap speculative candidate for packaged switchgear, transformer-integrated distribution and microgrid power, requiring strict balance-sheet, capacity and order-quality verification.
ESP should remain a low-confidence speculative magnetics/power-conversion shadow candidate unless commercial grid, data-center, energy-storage or microgrid customer exposure is found.

Need primary-source company filings, earnings transcripts, investor presentations and contract announcements for every ticker in this chunk; the supplied evidence mainly supports theme-level bottlenecks, not company-level revenue materiality.
Need current market-cap, revenue segment, backlog, customer concentration and analyst-coverage data before final underfollowed classification, especially for PPSI, ESP, GHM, LTBR and ASPI.
Need reference-company comparison against LEU for enrichment/HALEU, PLPC for transmission hardware, and established grid/EPC names for MTZ before ranking this chunk in the broader Energy funnel.

summary: Mapped the candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships for the Energy theme, with emphasis on nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks, dispatchable-power balance-of-plant, grid/EPC execution capacity, and power-distribution equipment. The strongest relationship in this chunk is BWXT as a reference nuclear-services and deconversion/feedstock candidate, but materiality to HALEU remains unproven from the supplied evidence. The most underfollowed/speculative relationships are GHM, PPSI, ESP, LTBR, and ASPI, each requiring primary-source validation before surviving later Serenity layers. MTZ is a reference execution-capacity beneficiary, but less pure and less underfollowed than smaller niche candidates.
